utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your mother tongue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, my name is Jan Wubben lead counsel for the Prosecution. Also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. I'm here together with co-counsel, Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends. I'm Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I appear on behalf of Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us today our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our case manager Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you and your team. A couple of things. We have reedited the CD-ROM containing the photos of the site visit, eliminating those that had nothing to do as such or which were of no importance to the proceedings, and including some other photos from my collection, for example. I asked that it be distributed to you in advance so that you would then come with a feedback as to whether that can enter into the records as an exhibit. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I took a look after being provided with the CD, and when it comes to the issue of being an exhibit, I really wonder how productive it will be when it also includes photographs of cows, vehicles, lunches during the site visit, a landing of a helicopter, the inside of a helicopter, and the burned log in the forest in the shape of some animal. These kind of photographs, I think, might be excluded from something like an exhibit. But, Your Honours, if the purpose is also to clarify the photographs as such, then it might be supportive as well to provide also a kind of overview of the specifications of the names of the villages or the river or the site that has been shown. That's my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jones or Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objection to those photographs being included as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. What we are going to do is -- I'll ask Mr. Blumenstock to reedit it, eliminating some of the photos that Mr. Wubben seems not to wish to see in the CD and then we will resubmit it to you. All right. Next thing is we will be handing down the -- our written decision on the Defence motion for protective measures. Since Witness D001 appears to be sort of the next one in the revised list, we are just telling you for the time being that our decision as regards this witness will be to grant the protective measures sought, namely pseudonym, facial and voice distortion, but not the late disclosure of the -- of the name of the witness to the Prosecution. So it's only this last protective measure that is not granted. Any other preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So I think we can then proceed with the testimony Mr. Sead Bekric. Usher, could you please go next to him. But he doesn't need to stand up. Just in case he needs either attention with the headphones or -- Mr. Bekric, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Throughout the proceedings, you will be receiving interpretation of what is being said in your language, or in a language that you understand. I take it you understand. If at any time there are problems with interpretation, say, either if you're not receiving interpretation or you notice the level is too high or too low which sometimes happens, please draw our attention straight away and we will rectify the problem or address it to the best of our abilities. Since you have a problem with your seeing, an impairment with your sight, I will be doing, together with the other two judges, our utmost to make life easy for you while you are giving testimony here. I have already made arrangements after consultation with the two judges to facilitate your being in the courtroom before everyone else so that you would feel at ease without having cameras showing you walk in and walk out. We agreed to have you be accompanied by your dog. For your information, I am the Presiding Judge and my name is Carmel Agius and I come from the Mediterranean island of Malta. To my right I have a Judge from the Kingdom of Denmark and his name is Hans Henrik Brydensholt, and to my left I have a Judge from Germany, from the Republic of Germany, and he is Professor Albin Eser, Judge Professor Albin Eser. Together we are presiding over this trial of Naser Oric the Defence of whom has summoned you as one of its witnesses. You will very soon start testifying, but before I proceed any further, I need to -- I wish to apologise to you for having kept you waiting for almost one hour now. The reason was a technical one due to a -- a technical shortcoming anyway, which we have solved and which needed time to be solved. We are now in a position to proceed, but before you start giving evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration to this Trial Chamber that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. It's kind of an oath that many witnesses take in many jurisdictions. I will be reading out this solemn declaration bit by bit to you. I'm reading it in English, it will be translated to you in Serbo-Croat, and I would like to you repeat in your own language --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honour. The witness will be testifying in English and using English throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I heard him answer me in English but I didn't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry. I should have pointed that out, including the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may say, Your Honour, I had the miss read to -- read me the solemn declaration in the waiting room and I have memorised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She read it to me a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's splendid, Mr. Bekric. Perhaps then you can remain seated and you can proceed with the solemn declaration immediately and that will be your solemn undertaking with us and then we can start.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Bekric, that is your solemn declaration and very briefly now, Mr. Jones, I take it, will be putting to you a series of questions. He will then be followed by Mr. Wubben who is lead counsel for the Prosecution. I don't know when we are expected to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was thinking that I would probably only need a day but given the delay it may be I go into part of tomorrow but the estimate which was originally five hours has been revised by me to 3 and a half hours, four hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the probability, Mr. Bekric, is that you will be with us again tomorrow morning. And then you will be free to go back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, before I forget, as regards your revised witness list, please, by the end of the week, Mr. Jones, please be kind enough to indicate the length of the expected testimony or the expected length of the testimony of each of those 30 witnesses, please, so that we can organise ourselves better and also the Defence -- the Prosecution team will be able to do that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. He wants to take them off? It's okay with me. Otherwise perhaps it's better -- possibly another better solution would be to leave them on and switch on channel 4, which is English, and that way he can always hear better what is being said. You see, I don't think he heard what I said. Examined by Mr. Jones:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning from me, Mr. Bekric and apologies from me too for the delay.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you to leave a bit of a pause between my question and your answer because we will be speaking in the same language so if you could make an effort to do that. Now, could you start by giving the Court your full name.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: My name is Sead Bekric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your date of birth is 30th of September 1978?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born in Voljevica, Bratunac municipality, Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your father's name was Selmen?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Bekric, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your mother's name was Mulja?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us firstly how you lost your sight.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was a soccer field in Srebrenica on April 12th 1993 and there was a massive amount of people and we had a match and there was a shelling from Zvijezda, from the hill above Bratunac and the soccer field was shelled and I was blinded, together with 62 other people killed on the soccer field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, after you were blinded in that mortar attack, were you evacuated to Tuzla and then to the United States?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was taken from the soccer field to Srebrenica hospital and then from Srebrenica hospital on to Tuzla and then from Tuzla I was transported to United States.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it right that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's just a matter of approach by my learned friend. He certainly wants to put words into the mouth of the witness but now he already started with a mortar attack and I tried to identify where the witness said something like that. But anyway, I see it is a triggering from my side to be precise and to advise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He referred to a shelling. A shelling is the same thing as a mortar attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The importance of the whole incident is in relation to how he ended up being blinded. Otherwise it's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's why I didn't intervene but it is more or less an advice to pay attention to the fact that don't use words that a witness didn't use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Wubben. Yes, Mr. Jones, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you were in the United States -- well, I presume I can lead on some background matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine. Usually you know what the practice is in this Tribunal. We allow you to lead, both sides, when in chief, except when there is an objection, which we will go into and decide accordingly. I mean -- so unless there is an objection, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certain matters in particular, you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm concerned my learned friend might object if I lead that this witness learnt Braille, but I don't know else to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it right that you learned Braille in a short space of time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, when I got to United States I started school without speaking the language, without knowing how to be blind, without learning Braille so I had to learn Braille mighty quick. So I learned Braille in two weeks, together with other equipment that is used for people with no vision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you learn English as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had to learn English as soon as possible because I was like a newborn child in a world without speaking it and without understanding what people around were saying so I had to learn mighty quick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it right that you graduated from high school and then university in the United States?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's right. I graduated from high school, regular high school, with 2.000 students who were all able to see and I graduated with honours and I got my degree recently, Bachelor's degree in international relations and global affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you also been involved with the American Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in the United States, I did not know what happened to my father after I left Srebrenica so my interest was to work with the American Red Cross to possibly have mail sent to him, to Srebrenica, and I asked them, you know, I'm blind, can I help volunteer to possibly get the information back to my family in Srebrenica? And they kindly accepted me even though I was blind and I worked a lot with the American Red Cross on many different programmes through three or four years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also involved with the Volunteers of America, I think they are called?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a National Youth Council of America with the American Red Cross and I worked on the organisation that Colin Powell started, the Volunteers of America.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally - this is all just background, obviously - what are your current plans?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I just graduated from college and on October 1 I'm taking LSAT law school exam and I'm hoping to go to law school next year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to take you back to the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is it right that when the war started, you were in Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you hear the suggestion of the interpreter, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We are being reminded, Mr. Bekric, to leave a pause between the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take it very slowly, that's fine. Did you grow up in Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for our benefit we are going to be looking at a map to follow your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So we have copies of the map we are going to be using for everyone which we will pass around at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally for the record because this had caught my eye before, but I preferred to wait. In page 7 line 6 the place of birth or the town of village of town of birth of the accused is [Realtime transcript read in error: "Valvica"] when it should be Voljevica. Page 7, line 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For this map I suggest it's a benefit for us but that we mark as we go along the places which are mentioned. I'm going to start with Voljevica. Firstly can you tell me the ethnic composition of Voljevica before the war.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Voljevica was majority Muslim but it had some inhabitants of Serbian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Bjelovac from Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Bjelovac from Voljevica is about three or four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Bjelovac much before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about Pobrdje. What was the ethnic composition of Pobrdje before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Pobrdje was majority Serb but it had some Muslim inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct just in terms of geography that Voljevica has the Drina on one side and then hills on the other side?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there a hill between Voljevica and Pobrdje?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is. The hill was called Vis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm marking that on my map and the various, some hills may not be actually -- may not appear on the map so I suggest we mark them as we go along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a hill called Caus?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. Caus is mountain or hill that was between Voljevica and that area and Srebrenica area, above Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say Srebrenica area, are you referring to the town or the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Srebrenica and the town, so whole area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Have you ever been to -- have you ever cared to - when of course before you had lost your eyesight - to see if you could see Caus, this hill Caus, from say Potocari, from Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Definitely you could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it visible from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Jones -- I pointed this out. No, no, no. Whether this hill Caus is visible from Potocari. In other words, if you look at -- if you're standing on the ground in Potocari, looking towards the direction of the Drina River, whether you can see this hill called Caus. This is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see Caus from Potocari area and from Voljevica area. It's one of the biggest peaks, biggest hills in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm saying this because this was pointed out to us in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We were asked to look at it anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are there any hills between Vis and Caus?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is. There is a hill above Pobrdje called Tablja and then goes on Zaluzje and then it connects up to Caus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, sorry again to interrupt you, but don't you have a better map than this? Because there is not even a survey map as such. If we could have a -- map of this particular area which would indicate these hills. I mean I think it will serve your purpose better and help us better definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour? In fact this -- in my submission this is actually an extremely useful map because practically all the village and hamlet place names which we are interested in here. It's just the names of a few of these hills which I'm dealing with at the outset and it has to be said that often hills have local names which may not appear on a national -- part of a national cartographic survey. You will notice that there are indications of hills next to Caus. There is one which case 488 metres I presume and there is another one between Pobrdje and Voljevica which says 384. It would be my submission that those -- those correspond to the hills which this witness is referring to, but I'm really not aware whether there is a map which would have all those names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My purpose -- I've been marking the hills as I go along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now are those places you mentioned, Vis, Tablja and Jelah, are they all on one ridge or are they arranged in some other way?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There is a ridge that goes all the way from Voljevica to Vis and connects up to Tablja. It's all one ridge and goes to Jelah and connects up to Caus area the hill of Caus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you mentioned Bjelovac. What was the ethnic composition of Bjelovac before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In Bjelovac, there is Serbian population, Muslim and Romas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zaluzje, what was its ethnic composition before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Zaluzje was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war broke out in Bosnia, were you aware of any tensions in the Voljevica area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was aware in the beginning of the war, when they had the elections, first of all they had the graffiti around Bratunac area, SDS graffiti, SDA and HDZ graffitis. And then there was election going on and my father was not allowed -- because my father moved from Srebrenica municipality before war to Voljevica and he was not allowed to vote because he bought land from Serbian neighbour. So he was not allowed to vote in Voljevica area so he was forced to go to vote in Pobrdje, in SDS club.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year would that be, those elections?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That was in -- I can't be specific how many months before war but not very long before war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when your father went to the SDS club to vote?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The -- our neighbour, that I knew was very good friends with my father from Pobrdje, Nikola Ostojic [phoen] told him, Selmen, what are you doing here? You're not supposed to be here, this is SDS club, you cannot vote for SDA or any other parties in this club. So my father did not get to vote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of any preparations for war in the Voljevica area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was. I was aware. A few months before war started, there was a preparations in Voljevica and there was a JNA and troops and reservists practising in the Voljevica area and they had their base in a school in Voljevica. The school of Voljevica, there were -- they had the main headquarters. That's where was about 50 to 70 troops based in the school and many more around hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to reservists, do you know where the reservists were from?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I recognised a lot of my neighbours from Pobrdje who were like I said in the past were good friends with my father. And many others came from our understanding were JNA troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that they were practising in the Voljevica area, can you explain a little more what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, they had the headquarters in the school. That's where they had the heavy weapons. Cannons, four-barrel anti-aircraft guns, anti-aircraft machine-guns in their kitchen and where the troops slept in the school and around the hills around Vis, around Krstas hill, and all around the hills, around Voljevica, there was troops in camouflage uniforms, dressed with the helmets, with the boots, with the full combat uniforms with light and heavy weapons in their hands, rocket-propelled grenades, Zoljas, AK-47s, automatic rifles. And there was another group also they were dressed in blue uniforms and then green khaki JNA uniforms all around hills in Srebrenica -- Bratunac, Voljevica, probably in the schools probably around 50 to 70 troops and hills around 2 or 300 all over the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a hill called Krstas. Can you tell us roughly what village or hamlet that is near?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Krstas is a hill that separates Bjelovac area and Voljevica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact just looking at the map there is a place Zaluzje, Prisoj, Biljaca. Is it near any of those places?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Krstas is above Zaluzje and the other side of the hill there is Prisoj, Bjelovac, Biljaca, and other side is Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described these troops practising in the hills around Voljevica. Is that something you yourself saw at the time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did because I was young kid who was interested in what was going on and I ran around with the troops, they took me around with them. They even gave me to clean their guns after they shoot them. I cleaned their guns. They gave me food. And I ran around all over the place with the troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the tensions which you referred to involving your father, that incident, did those sorts of things have any effect on the local population, the local Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Definitely did, because the -- as we know, that situation was -- was going on in Vukovar, Croatia and the propaganda was on television and people in Voljevica were afraid what was going to happen to them. You know, why these preparations, why guns, why uniforms, why around villages, you know. And people were afraid what's going to happen to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've referred to propaganda on television. Was there anything else which contributed to these fears?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because there was -- we knew that paramilitary from Arkan and Seslj were in the Bijeljina area, you know, spreading all over the place and many people from Bratunac, Serb authorities, came into Voljevica and they took a lot of men for questioning into Bratunac area or wherever they took them to, some which were beaten, some never returned. And there is another incident which spread the fear everywhere on Voljevica when Serbian troops brought two bodies into Voljevica and shot them right in middle of the village, sending a signal to us: Cooperate or this is -- was going to happen to you. I saw both those bodies shot right through the forehead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the people who were shot?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I found out those people from Glogova, last name Ibisevic and they were buried in Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What if anything did Muslims do as a result of these fears and these activities?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Male members of Voljevica were very afraid what's going to happen to them, will this same thing happen to them? So the result was that that we had to run into the hills, into the trees, into the woods, forest and hide in camp at night so for the fear that they might come and pick next men and take them, you know, to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, can he be specific now as the time when this -- whether they have arrived at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour, to ask that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was that? Can you place it either with a month and a year or in relation to other events?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That was about a month before Voljevica fell. So that was approximately in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did Voljevica fall?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I can't be specific date but it was mid-May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if it was suggested to you that Muslims left their homes and farms because they wanted to attack the Serbs from the woods, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll definitely disagree with that statement because I was there, I saw it, and I stayed behind after Voljevica fell. So when Voljevica -- when Serb troops especially my neighbours from Pobrdje I definitely saw they were good friends with my father and with the other troops surrounded whole area of Voljevica, whole hills around and they used megaphones and demanded to surrender all the weapons that the Muslims had in Voljevica. So we cooperate and there was no chance for us to fight with Serbs. First of all we did not have weapons. Second of all, Serbs came into Voljevica, expelled the people, cleansed the people from Voljevica and burned the whole village down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to disarming of Muslims in Voljevica. When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That happened in May, 1992, maybe five to seven days before we were expelled from Voljevica. Serb troops from Pobrdje across the Vis hill and from Andrici which is a village above in the Vezovac area and from Caus, Jelah, came from all different directions surrounded the village and also there was tanks and APCs positioned in the Serbia Jelah area facing Voljevica. We were surrounded and trucks came to Voljevica and with megaphones, demanded surrender or -- when we saw the -- our neighbours from Pobrdje area my father asked Nikola Ostolic and other neighbours that is we saw, What's going on, why you armed? Why you dressed in uniforms? What's going to happen to us here? And his reply was, We are here to protect you, not here to harm anybody. Two days later, the whole village was cleansed and burned to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were weapons handed in?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: My grandfather handed his registered shotgun and other -- all other Muslim male members who had registered weapons, which the Serbs had of course on the record all the registered weapons, were turned into Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where specifically in Voljevica the weapons had to be handed in?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, those weapons were handed in by the school in Voljevica. The truck came there and all weapons were handed in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the school which you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to tell the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to tell that -- draw that to the witness's attention because he's not wearing earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We are just being reminded that we need to leave more of a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Okay, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's not in dispute that Bosnian Serb forces attacked Muslim villages and that there was a policy of ethnic cleansing. I'm referring that's areas 2 and 4 in Your Honours decision. So I'm not going to ask but that in detail just a few details to establish your movements. Did there come a time when Muslim villages in Bratunac fell to Serb forces, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. In -- right before Voljevica fell. I can't be specific but around month or so before we got news in Voljevica that Glogova fell to Serbian forces and was ethnically cleansed and then Suha which is in Bratunac area was also ethnically cleansed and burned to the ground and Mihajlevici also, which I watched myself burned before we were -- before we were ethnically cleansed from Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see Mihajlevici burn?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was on the hill right below Vis and we can see over there the area of Mihajlevici and we saw houses, flames, smoke, burning and we can see livestocks in the meadows in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to get to these places by road once you mentioned Suha, Mihajlevici, Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: No we could not because in -- on the border between Voljevica and Pobrdje there was a barricade right there on the road. You could not cross toward Bratunac. Many attempts were made from people from Bjelovac, Biljaca, Tegare, to go toward Bratunac and they were stopped at - -many of them were taken and never saw; many of them were taken and beaten. And when we saw what happened to them nobody attempted because, you know, those troops right there on the road. You could not cross it. And then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you something? Those troops who were manning those barricades, were they Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: They were our neighbours from Pobrdje, from Pobrdje area. Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people who were being stopped and taken away were what ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Those were Muslims who were already expelled from their villages up toward the Tegare area and some expelled went towards Mocevici village and some tried to go toward Bratunac and they were stopped there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned Glogova, Mihajlevici, Suha. Are there any other Muslim villages which you're aware of which were burnt or attacked?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then Zaluzje burned, Bjelovac burned, Biljaca burned and Sase burned at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Bjelovac. When did that burn, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Bjelovac burned around same time, a little bit before Voljevica burned. We were in Voljevica when Zaluzje was burning and when Biljaca and Sase were burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which part of Bjelovac was burning?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The whole commune. Whatever they had the Muslim population who successfully went out of the Bjelovac before, was lucky for them their houses burnt and those who were not -- could not leave Bjelovac they ran to the hills and their houses were immediately burned after they were cleansed from their village. And the same thing applied to Biljaca and Sase and Prisoj area as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned several times Serbs from Pobrdje who you knew. Are there any names of specific Serbs whom you saw with your own eyes involved in these activities?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is. I saw Radomir Ostojic. I saw Sreten Lazic, his brother Mirko Lazic. Ivan Lazic, Teodor Lazic, Dragan Ostojic. And a lot of nicknames, I saw Mico Lazic, and I saw Milo Obrenovic. They were all our neighbours that we knew from the past who my father bought land from them and when I saw them, they were all dressed in the different uniforms, camouflage uniforms, with the rifles, with the blue uniforms and with the green khaki uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from Serbs from Pobrdje, were you aware of Serbs from any other Serb villages being involved in these operations?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the population of Voljevica was cleansed from Voljevica and they ran to the hills I stayed behind with my neighbour and his four sons. So we were hiding in the woods around Krstas. We saw Serbian troops coming toward -- from Prisoj and Bjelovac area and then from the bushes we saw them and my neighbour Ahmo Sukrija. And this is the Serb neighbour that is I used to work with and was friends with before the war from Bjelovac and that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were in the hills in around Krstas. Can you just describe to us what sort of a view you had from Krstas from the surrounding villages and possibly Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: If you're standing in Krstas you can see whole surrounding area. You can see Voljevica area, you can see Lubovija which is across Drina River in Serbia and you can see Zaluzje, Bjelovac and that whole around area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us roughly when you were up in the hills around Krstas, for what period and for how long.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, we were in Krstas in the woods and trees before Voljevica fell, of course, because we were with the other male members hiding from the Serbian authorities and the troops coming into the town and then I also stayed after people Voljevica left or pushed out of Voljevica into the hills, I stayed behind with my neighbour Ahmo and four of his sons for a couple of days after the fall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period that you were up there, can you describe what if anything you saw in terms of military activity on either side of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I saw troops coming from my house, from the Vis area, down toward Voljevica and toward Krstas area. They were also my neighbours that I mentioned before. And then I also troops -- saw troops coming from Bjelovac area, all dressed in uniforms. And many trucks were loaded with the goods also coming from the road that led from Srebrenica on to Sase, Bjelovac into Bratunac, carrying all goods, furniture, televisions, refrigerators, all kind of goods were carried and being escorted by the small vehicles with the troops in them and with the rifles pointing at the village -- at the houses in the village of Voljevica as they passed through. And when Serbian troops came to burn Voljevica, they also had a lot of humongous trucks and tractors coming in there. The first they did they surrounded the village they had troops on every single hill, all fully equipped for combat with the weapons and all different kind uniforms, surrounded the village. And from Serbia, you can see APC right across the Drina River where I used to go swimming facing right at the Voljevica and the tank also was positioned in Serbia facing the Voljevica. When the Serbian troops entered Voljevica, they -- neighbours from my neighbouring village of Pobrdje and other Serbs from Bjelovac area and whole the commune came into Voljevica looted the whole place, took the -- whatever they wanted, took the livestocks, took the tractors that we had, trucks, cars, whatever they can find, took it toward Bratunac and toward Bjelovac and then they torched [Realtime transcript read in error: "tortured"] majority of the village to the ground. And I saw my own house burnt to the ground. And they took whatever livestocks we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I stop you there for one moment? Did you say they tortured the majority of the village to the ground or torched?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear the last part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's just a question for the transcript. It says that "they tortured majority of the village to the grounds and I saw my own house burnt to the down." Did you mean to say tortured or some other word?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Torched, like burned to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now at this time were -- was your family with you or were they were Voljevica or where were they?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When people from Voljevica were moving through the hills up towards Mocevici I sent my mother, my father and my little brother with the other people and I stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you mentioned livestock. Did you have livestock at that time your family?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes we had the sheep and goats and my neighbour who was -- who I was with, he had a horses, cows, sheep and other livestocks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at this time, you were 13 years old, I take it. Can you explain to us how you as a 13 year old were left alone in the hills or chose to be alone in the hills rather than going with your family?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, I had a little brother who was eight years old. I had a mother, sister, and I had a father who was sick. So I was -- I took over as a main person to support them. So when I sent them I was hoping that even though all people were cleansed from the village, we still hoped it was going to last for a couple of days and when I stayed behind I went to play role [phoen] my family hoping to -- you know, it's your home and save what we had. So when we saw what happened to our village, then I lost my hope. And then I did as everybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It might also help if you explain, if you can, your personality at the time. Were you shy or outgoing, adventurous, retiring? If you can give us just a sense of what your character was like at the time.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: My character was I was very active person who very young years learnt to do all kind of works. I always hang out with the older people. I never played with young kids. I really did not like playing different games like other kids. I was -- would go to with the older men, listen to the news, listen what they talk about, talk about days of work. And my personality was always hyper, always like the adventure, do things that nobody else liked to do. You know I would take my neighbour's horse, I would go ride around the hills. I would explore the hills, go see what's going on in the village, main part of village, so it was non-stop, non-stop going person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, just a little more on Voljevica, when that was burnt. What precisely actually did you see? Did you see -- well, if you could just describe for us what in fact you saw and how far away you were when you saw it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When -- if I understand the question, when the troops arrived in Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, when the village was burned.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the same neighbours as I mentioned before, across from my house down from the hill down toward my house. They burnt my house, that's my neighbours from Pobrdje. I saw troops from other side of Voljevica coming with the armed trucks with the automatic rifles, machine-guns, dressed in uniforms, when they surrounded Voljevica and when they started looting and burning the whole place down. And you can see -- hear the firing massive firing going on in the Caus area and Andrici area. You can hear automatic fire and very furious shelling which we understood was going toward Srebrenica area, toward Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just two more questions on that. You said neighbours were coming from Pobrdje, and then you said "I saw troops from other side of Voljevica." Can you tell us what village or hamlets would be on the other side of Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That would be coming -- I'm sorry. That would be coming from Bjelovac commune area and Sase area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of any smoke or flames which you saw, was that visible just locally or was that somebody that would be seen from further afield?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The smoke, I saw the burning house I saw in Mihajlevici that were burning. And I saw Voljevica burning. And then I also saw when I was crossing to Mocevici, fire in the Zaluzje area, fire in Bjelovac and Sase and Biljaca area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were able to see smoke in Bjelovac when were you in Voljevica. In your opinion would someone in Bjelovac be able to see smoke and flame in Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims in Voljevica when it fell?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was a couple of elderly people left there and there was a police officer I think it was Mujo, before, he was a police officer before the war. He was captured there, taken, and from my understanding he was tortured, beaten and never saw again. And there was another guy, his name was Sefko, he was taken, forced to burn mosque, put an explosive and burn mosque down in Voljevica. And my grandmother and my grandfather stayed behind because they were elderly and they were based in a house in Voljevica, together with the seven or eight other people. And my father -- grandfather and grandmother went to look for food and as soon as they left the house, the whole house was set on fire and everybody in there burnt to the ground, was eight people. And from -- what my grandfather told me and my grandmother, who they saw was Radomir Ostojic from Pobrdje was dressed in uniform with the machine-gun who put explosives and grenades into the house and burned it to the ground with all those people, all the people -- old people in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't need to tell us the names but do you know the names of the people who were in the house?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when you too left the Voljevica area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was. It was a few days after Voljevica was burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you alone or did you go with others?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was with my neighbour Ahmo and four of his sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you head for?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We went toward village of Mocevici. We had to cross from Krstas to Prisoj and though very dangerous terrain and very dangerous what we call death valley in Biljaca and up toward Pozlodnik into Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to Biljaca in a moment. I'm not sure if you told us where you were headed for, if there was any specific village.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We did not have in our mind specific village where we were heading but -- because we did not know what's going to happen next day, will that village be burnt to the ground also. But from our understanding we were heading to village of Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you encounter any other people on the way there or did you arrive there on your own with your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When we crossed Biljaca up toward Pozlodnik you can see thousands and thousands of people scattered all over the hills, all over the meadows, in the barns, in the houses, children screaming, fires everywhere, trying to hear families. You know, people were from all different villages that were from low ground at Drina valley. Every single meadow, every single woods were packed with thousands of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these people Serbs or Muslims or something else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: This is the Muslim population that was cleansed from low grounds, from Drina valley, from Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- okay. Now, you mentioned Biljaca and I think you called it death valley. Before the war, what was the ethnic composition of Biljaca?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Biljaca was majority Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, were there Muslims still in Biljaca?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: No. When we crossed Biljaca, Biljaca was totally burned, torched to the ground, together with Prisoj and Bjelovac and Sase area. And of course you've got Biljaca and Zaluzje there also which was torched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Biljaca from Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Biljaca from Bjelovac is about three to four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you take that route out of the Voljevica area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We had no other options. Bratunac, the road toward Bratunac was blocked. We could not go because as I mentioned Serbian troops from Pobrdje blocked that road. The Caus area that we could cross toward Srebrenica was furious shelling and fighting going on which Serbs already took over took the positions in that those hills. And road that went up toward Sase into -- towards Srebrenica was already taken over by Serbs and they had positions there. That was already burnt. So even the road that we -- the trail that we took was not safe at all but we had to cross it in the very late hours and night to cross the very dangerous road in Biljaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just a question of clarification towards my learned friend. He's using a map provided to us and to indicate for myself, also following the witness testimony, I don't know what the scale of it is, of the map. Is it right to say that a square in -- within the map is one kilometre and a half? So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That will clarify a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: One moment, please. The scale is 1 to 100.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One kilometre for every square.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: A square is not one centimetre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to agree to anything like that unless we all get our rulers out. The scale is 1 to 100.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The scale is more than one centimetre here. I would say it's about two centimetres, but I'm not sure either.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, if I may be allowed to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We will find out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could be 1.5, as you say, actually. It could be one square 1.5 because it's quite possible that will a square is 1 point centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps rather than talk about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can check that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bekric, the distance from Biljaca to Bjelovac, leaving aside kilometres, how long would it take you walking to get from Bjelovac to Biljaca?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: As I was at that time, I could see and the way I was I could probably run it in ten, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you travel on that road in your youth?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Before war, I used to go there all time bike riding toward Bjelovac, towards Sase, toward all different areas there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would it take you on bicycle from Biljaca to Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Five minutes, maybe even that much, five minutes at most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that I believe your evidence is that you crossed the road by Biljaca. Was it safe to cross that road?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That road, we had a nickname for it, we called death valley because when we crossed from Krstas toward Biljaca to Prisoj I crossed the way right above Bjelovac. There was a hill Kunjarac, and they had a very deathly weapons there which was a machine-guns, anti-aircraft guns, and it was probably as the crow flies from Prisoj above Biljaca that we had to cross, it was probably a kilometre or so, maybe even less. So when we descended on toward Biljaca, there was always troops, Serbian troops from Sase and from Bjelovac up and down waiting for Muslims to cross the area and if you cross at Vezovac you're dead right there and I know many my friends from Voljevica that were killed there and many were captured, never saw -- seen again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, did you ever go up Kunjarac hill yourself?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've gone to Kunjarac -- I mean I was there before war and I've seen Kunjarac also during the war when the action was taking place there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since kilometres may or may not be a useful guide, how long will it take you to walk from Bjelovac to Kunjarac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: A few minutes, maybe five minutes, probably a distance of maybe between 300 and 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've referred to Plice [phoen] before. Was there anything at this time when you crossed the road to leave the Voljevica area, anything which you observed there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a shooting, automatic machine-gun shooting from Kunjarac, a lot of shooting going on in Bjelovac area and you can see the smokes going on, smoke, like burning. I can't be specific whether it was a house or barn or some -- it was a huge flames going on in Bjelovac, in Sase area also. There was a lot of burning and firing from every single direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Eser would like to put a question at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to make sure, because I can't find Kunjarac on the map. Could you perhaps describe: Is it direction to Kostanovice or direction to Gradina or to some -- is it closer to Prisoj?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've marked it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help just to locate Kunjarac in relation to Bjelovac, Prisoj, and --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. If you see on the map Bjelovac and you see Biljaca, so it's between you see it's the hill between -- it's right above Bjelovac and between Biljaca and Bjelovac. It's right immediately above Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it on the Voljevica side of the road or on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The other side at the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Bjelovac itself did you see any military presence or activity?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I've seen military presence in Bjelovac right before war started when I used to go, we had like a small village club in Sase area. So I used to go there, was gathering. And I rode a bike toward Sase and Bjelovac, you can see presence of dressed soldiers with uniforms with the AK-47s, with the automatic rifles, and there were even getting on the buses where the villagers who were going through right before the war started. And then also when we were in Sase at the -- in the village club, there was a spray of automatic shooting from Andrici area so we were forced to disperse from that place and run in every single directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Sase, what was its ethnic composition before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In Sase it was mixed but majority of Sase, I believe, is Muslim. I got -- you have villages around Sase commune the majority were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that road you described going up to Biljaca and then up to Sase, in May 1992, could you take that road to get to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because first of all you could not cross if you were coming from Voljevica. In Bjelovac you could not go towards Sase. It was blocked. And the trail that we took toward Biljaca, you could not take it because they -- all the killings that happened in Biljaca were from Serbs coming down patrolling the area from Sase and from Bjelovac and Muslim population in Sase were already ethnically cleansed and burned -- their houses burned to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to deal now with Mocevici. Whether you arrived there, did you finds any other people there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When I arrived to Mocevici there were thousands of people in every single place you can look at. It's like sketches everywhere. And all the houses in Mocevici were packed with the refugees and my aunt had -- my aunt's husband had a family in Mocevici and that's where I was located, and where I found my family there. And every single place, every single corner was packed with refugees. And you know, it was -- at night gets very cold and the people like myself and my family, we only had what we could carry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what were the Serb villages, if any, which were in the immediate area of Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes in the surrounding Mocevici area there was Oparci, there was other side, Spat, and then towards Osmace -- I mean towards Srebrenica there is Pribicevac there is Brezani in the direction of Osmace and there's Radijevci, in that area to where immediately close to Mocevici and other villages down below. There is Sikirici and so on, their commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "below," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: If you -- if you have a map and if you look at where Mocevici is and right above other side, there is also Brezovica and Pozlodnik also. And right cross on the other side there is a hill called Oparci and below Oparci there is Muslim village called Zapolje which was already ethnically cleansed and torched to the ground. And on those hills were heavy artillery based and heavy weapons that were continuously shooting towards refugees in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if someone were to say that in June 1992 -- first of all, when did you arrive in Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I arrived in Mocevici beginning of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if someone were to say that in that period Muslims were not unable but were going back and forthwith their cattle to the market in Fakovici, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That would be absolutely impossible. Where the refugees were pushed in that rugged area we had no, absolutely, possibility to go down toward the river, towards Drina in any kind direction. Not toward Sikiric, not toward Fakovici, not toward Voljevica. Not toward any single direction. We were completely up in the mountains, in the hills, surrounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Facing the other direction, were Muslims able to get to Srebrenica through Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely no, not. Because we had no contact whatsoever with Srebrenica at that time. People panicking, you know, what was going to happen, because we were cleansed from our villages and we had no contact with the outside world. Like, if you went to Srebrenica you could not contact nobody. We didn't even know what the fate was, what's going on in Srebrenica. We didn't know what was going on around us and we knew that very stronghold in Pribicevac was there that was blocking our crossing towards Srebrenica. And toward Osmace, there is Brezani. You could hear continuous shooting and shelling from Brezani area and Pribicevac. On other side, where I was close to is Mocevici where I was staying in. Other side there is Oparci, hill of Oparci, which was continuously non-stop shooting in that area toward refugees in those hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, one moment. I would like to know whether he is in a position to tell us at least whether at this time when he arrived in Mocevici, Mocevici was connected by telephone with the rest of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, if Mocevici was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was connected by telephone, whether there was telephone connection, telephone lines in Mocevici connected to the rest of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mocevici is a very, very hilly area. Even before the war there was no chance by having telephone in that area. Not those villages in that area had telephones, not even the village where I was in which was very flat and very close to Bratunac, very close to Serbia, had telephone lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the situation -- actually firstly for clarity maybe it doesn't need clarification but referring to Pribicevac and Brezovica, are these -- you described Pribicevac as a stronghold. Are these Serb areas or Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: It was Serbian areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Radijevici. What was the situation in relation to Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: If you look at that area, like as I mentioned before, Oparci village area and all those other villages surround that area and down below there is a Sikiric, and those Oparci and Radijevici and those other villages in that area I had no other way to get support. It was continuous, continuous fighting, shooting coming from that area, shelling and anti-aircraft shooting coming from that area and they had Mocevici above them and the only way they could got support is down from below which is Sikirici. And that's -- from where I know that is from talking to my neighbours from my village who were in the Mocevici area. They were discussing how Serbs in that area having all these weapons, where they getting it from and the discussion was that they getting it down below from Sikirici area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a place called Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ratkovici is in that area also, Ratkovici was in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that Serb or Muslim at this time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That was Serb village. Everybody feared Ratkovici, that area there. Because the fear was the Serbs already have Bjelovac, Serbs have the area Sase and Voljevica and all along the Drina valley. If they continue pushing from that side from Sikiric and from Oparci and from Haliljovici, then if Mocevici falls then the thousands and thousands of people would be endangered. There have no place to go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, as far as the information about those fears, about Ratkovici and the situation for those in Mocevici was concerned, what was your source for that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's from talking to my neighbours, because as I said before, I was always intruder, liked to listen to what all the men talk so I go around the village first I saw my neighbour Ahmo and his sons and they would be discussing with the other men what's going to happen to them and what was going on and that was my source. They were discussing between each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in Mocevici, was there any sort of Defence organised among the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: From when I was in Mocevici, there was Vekas Husic who was from Mocevici, who organised defence from all the men from Mocevici. And when men arrived from other villages that were cleansed arrived in Mocevici area, he organised them to stand guard around Mocevici and that area from -- between Muslims and Serbs where the shooting was coming from the Oparci area especially, and Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's just being pointed out to me for the transcript it's Vekas Husic. But we can correct those names at the end as well as Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now did the men who you saw and who were involved in the defence in Mocevici, did they have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. The people the thousands -- the people from my own village, the people that I used to see every day. That was the people who scared people, weak people, who were ethnically cleansed to the -- to the rugged hills where they had nothing and no one that they know in those villages. They were there and they were told they must stand guard to protect it. They had -- just like we do, jeans or ragged pants or any kind of rubber shoes, T-shirt. That was what was known as defender of the area. And whatever weapons they had they had to use it. It was not even possibility to identify those people as soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these men going into action when you were there in Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I've seen people from my village and other villages going to take over very strong hill of Oparci which they attempted a few times, no success to take over because there was no match between anti-aircraft gun and a shotgun so it was a lot of wounded and dead being carried through but there was no success taking over that hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a question about Osmace. Are you familiar with Osmace?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, do you know whether that was physically connected to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Because Osmace the road that was going from Kragljevoda towards Vlasenica is a road that goes through Kragljevoda to Zeleni Jadar and to Vlasenica military area was already taken by Serbs and was a very strong Serbian positions in Brezani which was impossible to cross to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you -- whether you were in Mocevici did you actually return to Voljevica at any stage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard people from my village discussing return to regain food or supplies because nobody had nothing. And I told my mother that was they going to prepare the trip to try to regain food. And my mother and I went with the other people from my village to the hills toward Voljevica, same way that we came from, and we got to Voljevica. The trip was from hell. You had to travel dark hours. You couldn't use any torch or light or nothing whatsoever. So basically you got to walk as a crow, very slow and then descend to Biljaca and then on to Voljevica. When we got to Biljaca -- whether the Serbs knew we were there or not, we crossed Prisoj from Biljaca into Prisoj. There was a very fierce shooting coming from Kunjerac area toward Prisoj. So we will had to like lay there for hours waiting for it's over. I cannot say they knew we were there or that was their routine. So when we got to Voljevica, I could not get to my house up there because of the dangers. That's where Serb positions were, above the house. And I went to my neighbour's house and I got some food from there with my mother and we met and slowly through the hills returned to very dangerous area and mined area towards Mocevici again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did there come a time when you left Mocevici for good?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was talking to my -- my neighbour Ahmo and his sons, and they stay at this guy's house his name is Sukrija. He's from Stozersko. He was -- he introduced -- people discussing what's going to happen to the people, where do we go from here? And when these Sukrija guy introduced himself he said I'm a fighter from Hakija Meholjic's defence force it was organised. I can attempt to guide you guys to Srebrenica. I haven't been there, I'm not from there. I can attempt to take you but you're going to take your chances, same as I do. If somebody happens to me it's going to happen to you. So we can attempt it. So we had no other choices: Stay there in the cold open air or attempt to cross into Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt the journey?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We took the trip with Sukrija being the guide on to through Mocevici, Predola, Stozersko and Skenderovici. And then we had to cross a canyon which is very, very, very steep in the middle of the day. You could not see nothing that's how dark it is. It's a very rocky area and between Zeleni Jadar and Pribicevac. So we started descending into the canyon, when Serbs discovered us. And there was a very, very dangerous road to cross -- the canyon to cross and when they start firing at us from anti-aircraft machine aircraft -- anti-aircraft machine-gun and all different weapons at us, that's when people start screaming and running all different directions. And my little brother was starting to run in all different directions from where I was, and I had to run after him to calm him down. And that's when I saw first time in Kunjerac with wounded people and screaming people, mothers, children, bags everywhere, and then I took my brother and we ran towards Srebrenica to the hills, left my father and my mother in canyon and we made it to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was -- when was this, firstly, more or less?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this approximately, the day?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That was in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Srebrenica like whether you found it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I used to be -- I used to go to Srebrenica before war. I had a sister lived in Srebrenica municipality. Srebrenica used to be a very small town, very happening town with small cafes, restaurants, coffee shops. And when we arrived in Srebrenica it was like a ghost town, dead, no one there. I walked through the whole Srebrenica and I don't think I saw one person in the whole of Srebrenica. Many houses were torched, burned, looted, glass broken, the smell of smoke around Srebrenica. All the places that I used to know, boutiques, restaurants, cafes, everything was empty, looted, dead. Dead -- deadly town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was anyone organising anything in the town as far as you could tell? Was anybody receiving refugees or trying to organise them?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: From our understanding only person that had defence at that time when I -- we arrived was Hakija Meholjic. They had organised a defence force and -- when Serbs left Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, just to regulate yourself we have roughly another eight, ten minutes before we have a break so --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just keep that in mind and if we need to make it 10 or 12 we will make it 10 or 12 obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think I can finish in about eight minutes this subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We found a house right next to the hospital in Srebrenica. My family and another family got into the house and we stayed there for the time being, at the time I was in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of a PTT building in --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I knew about PTT before the war and during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that in relation to where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was maybe a hundred metres from the house, right across from hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in that house?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I stayed from June 1992 until I was blinded in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us who stayed in the house with you from the beginning through to April 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Srebrenica we had two families my family and another family. By the time I left Srebrenica there was probably about 50 people in the house. It was packed with people. And the house was disgustingly dirty. We didn't have no stoves. We didn't have no water, no electricity. Dirty, lice, all kinds of possibility, dirty people you could see was in that house. Not only that house but everywhere you go in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people, the 50 people, who were there with you, where were they from?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In that house where I was from we had people from Zvornik municipality, we had people from Zepa, we had people from Visegrad, we had people in Bratunac municipality, from every single place. From Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss amongst you what had happened and how you came to be in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have. And it's exactly same what happened to my people in my village. People from Zvornik municipality was over -- was exactly the same what happened to us. They were forced to surrender their weapons. Many people were -- who could escape escaped, many of them killed, many of them never returned their homes torched. That happened all the way from Zvornik to Bratunac municipality to Visegrad, Zepa and Vlasenica. All people that were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in Srebrenica, did you just stay in the house or did you move around the town or the area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
