utterances.text: I was a very curious kid, very rowdy kid, and I was also a very caring person who took care my family. So when my family came into Srebrenica, there was a -- we had no food whatsoever so I was forced to go around Voljevica -- around Srebrenica around the apartments, around the houses, look for food, for clothing, for anything I could find for my family to survive and talked to many people around Srebrenica who I know that arrived later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other relatives in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I had a sister who lived in Potocari area and I had a sister that lived in Ljeskovik which is south of Srebrenica, probably 15 to 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you try and see them?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in Srebrenica, my first thought was to cross towards my sister in Ljeskovik and to go see her so she can possibly give us -- because her village did not burn at that time. So we were hoping there can be possibility for me to cross to her village and possibly later on also bring my family there so when I spoke to people in Srebrenica, they said it would be impossible to cross it by regular road, you had to be very careful how you cross because Serbian troops all the roads that was leaving from Kragljevoda to Vlasenica was taken by Serbian troops and all the Muslim villages in that area were torched and the Serbian positions. And if you attempt it was impossible to cross it but if you attempt it you risking your life and you get across totally different direction than you would normally cross it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So be it be right that in the course of trying to see your sister and visiting relatives you became aware which areas were accessible and which areas were blocked?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's correct..

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become aware which persons or groups held different areas around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. That in the -- in the beginning of war, we know that in Srebrenica it was Hakija Meholjic and later on it was Akif Ustic. In the south part of the Srebrenica area there was Nedzad Bektic. And then also in Suceska, where my father is from, there was Tursunovic had his defence up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a good time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a 25 minute break. Usher, you need to organise the assistance for the witness. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's continue. Let's wait for the accused. All right. Let's continue. Sorry for the delay. Of course, Madam Registrar, the time lost will be accredited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bekric, before the break, you mentioned Hakija Meholjic. Where was he based?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Hakija Meholjic from my understanding from talking to people in Sukrija, from Stozersko, he was located outside Srebrenica in the hills at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he remain outside in the hills?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: No. He got sent down to Srebrenica soon as refugees started coming down into the town. The first group arrived when I arrived in -- other people with me, that's when Hakija Meholjic was in Srebrenica with his fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where in the town precisely were they based, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In Hotel Domavija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you Hakija and his fighters, you said that Sukrija was one of Hakija's men. What if anything did Hakija's men or fighters say about the defence of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: They from what I understood that Srebrenica was cut off from outside, there was no connection, no contact with the other hamlets and villages around. Hakija is the one who organised the defence of Srebrenica and he is going to be the commander of the forces in Srebrenica at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people, how many men, did -- were in Hakija's unit, if you know? This is -- I'm talking about June 1992 when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I would say anywhere between 200 to 300 soldiers, fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that number remain the same throughout 1992 or did it change?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, actually, in the beginning of the war, he did not have -- by the time I left Srebrenica I would say he had about 2 or 300 fighters. In the beginning what happened is when he had a few gathered men as a defence then many refugees from Bratunac municipality when they arrived joined Hakija Meholjic's group all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone from your village, Voljevica, join his unit?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes he had a few men from Voljevica joined Hakija Meholjic's group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of any of those men?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There was Hazim from Voljevica who was in his group, there was Muhamed from Voljevica who was in his group and in the beginning there was Omer in his group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Hazim from Voljevica have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. We called him Mercury before the war and after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to him in a moment. Did you hear talk about another group of fighters in the town of Srebrenica at this stage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, later on we also -- the group that is organising was Akif Ustic who organised his group after Meholjic and then continued time in Srebrenica was Akif with his troops until he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know roughly when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I would say late 1992 sometimes in the ambush in the village of Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned Hazim from Voljevica. Was he with Akif when he was killed or was he somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Sorry for cutting you off. Hazim from Voljevica was first in Hakija Meholjic's group and then him and Enver from Voljevica -- and another man from Voljevica, we called him Ibro, was in Akif Ustic's group and came also from Voljevica was in his group. And when Akif was ambushed, they were killed and Hazim from Voljevica escaped that ambush.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back to Hakija for a moment, were you aware of him being under any other commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say at that time, at any time, were you aware of him being placed under the command of any other commander?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Hakija Meholjic was one of the first who organised defence and he -- all through the time in Srebrenica when I was there Hakija had his group and he was based in Domavija and he did at his will what he wanted to do. He had no commander. Nobody could command Hakija Meholjic. If anybody considered himself commander it was Hakija Meholjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, how do you know what that? What's the basis for you saying that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Because a lot of the men like I said Hazim from Voljevica, Mercury was good friends with my father. He spoke to my father before the war and during the war. He would come see us and he would explain what was going on in Srebrenica who was the leader, who was the commander he was based and also another male members from my village who were talking was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Akif Ustic, same question: Were you aware of him being placed under any other commander at any stage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Akif Ustic and Hakija Meholjic were totally commanders and Akif had his group and Hakija Meholjic had his group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Zulfo Tursunovic, who had his defence up in Suceska, as you put it. Can you describe for us what Zulfo was like? Or firstly did you have occasion to encounter Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In time we arrived in Srebrenica and later on, when I attempted to go to Suceska to cross where my father was born, I've seen Zulfo and Zulfo had totally command of Suceska area all his men and villages Suceska. But there was no -- the road going to Suceska was not open at that time. You could not cross it. So I took my own risk, I took the risk to go to Suceska that's where I saw Zulfo. And also I know Zulfo before the war. He was a distant relative of my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually just one point out to clarify. You said how Zulfo had his defence up in Suceska. In the past you also talked about someone being down by the Drina. Just for clarification, when you say up and down are you referring to hills and valleys, or north, south? Just so we can be a bit clear.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When I say up in Suceska that means up in the hills of -- Srebrenica municipality. Up all the way up in the hills which I suppose to be western side of the enclave Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you also mentioned Nedzad Bektic. What area was he in again if you can remind us in that period June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: He was in the south part of Srebrenica in the Kragljevoda area. The first time I got to know who Nedzad Bektic was when I finally made attempt to cross -- when I made it to my sister's village, villages were talking about having a commander at that area was Nedzad Bektic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June 1992, was the -- was the -- this area connected to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The south part of Srebrenica was absolutely not connected because many refugees attempt to cross from that area toward Srebrenica it was impossible because Serbs had their front lines all the way from Kragljevoda on to toward Milici it was totally -- the road was completely blocked and they had their front lines there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in this period and indeed afterwards, in this second half of 1992, what were you doing to get food? How were you obtaining food?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When there was a -- first of all we attempted many times to go to our own villages to Voljevica through the hills around the Obadi and then on to Vezovac into Voljevica. Many attempts were made. Some made it. I made a couple of times to Voljevica. There was landmines everywhere and many people were wounded. Many people were killed many people were captured when we went to get the food. And then the time I got to also look for food when there was action like everybody else was. There was action for food. That's where you got food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it right that you were travelling around the enclave, around this area quite a bit in the second half of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was all over the place, all over the enclave. I don't think there's one part of the enclave I don't know. Every single corner, every single possibility to get food to travel through I done it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you know Naser Oric either during or before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I saw Naser Oric once or twice in Voljevica before war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you know of him and his situation, if anything, in June-July 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, in Voljevica before we were cleansed from Voljevica we heard that Arkan's paramilitary was attempting a huge attack on Potocari and that the people from Potocari were stopping him from crossing into Srebrenica where massive amount of people. Refugees were in the hills. And my understanding was not that people from Potocari stopped Arkan and his men and that Naser was there. That's the only thing I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then in June -- well, yes, when would that be with the Arkan's paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That was in beginning of the 1992, in the beginning of the war. And during the time in Srebrenica I did not see Naser at all until Philippe Morillon came with the UN peacekeepers in the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything of what was going on in Potocari with Naser Oric in June-July 1992 or later?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: First of all, I had a sister who lived in Potocari area. We could not cross to Potocari because a massive shelling continuously from Zaluzje and from Zaluzje, the hill above Bratunac and was shelling the roads and the hills between Srebrenica and Potocari. So it was impossible tore to us cross that area. But later on, we could have crossed -- late 1992 we knew that was when Potocari, we could cross there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any stage hear or were people saying in the town of Srebrenica that Naser Oric was the overall commander in the whole Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: People in the Srebrenica, when I say Srebrenica, people from Srebrenica municipality and from all other municipalities that were in Srebrenica refugees as refugees, no one had a commander as an overall commander and there was not, could have been a commander of all people in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Because what happened is if you are for example on the southeastern part of enclave you've got Nedzad Bektic and he's got his men up there. The villages followed him because he was the first one who stood up to the Serbian aggression. And then you got the other party from Bratunac municipality who had their own leaders and who they tried to organise defence to pass into their own villages. They did not look up to no commanders. They considered themselves their own commanders. And then you got other commanders like Hakija Meholjic who had his own group and he considered himself a commander and he commanded his own group. No one could command him. And then you had Tursunovic who had his own group and he commanded himself. No one could command him. And people the way people were spread in enclave is like people from the parts, you know. You have a leader, you stood up to the first aggression, and then everybody admired you and they followed you. And besides, in at the beginning of the war, you know, to late 1992 there was no connection whatsoever to the other parts of the villages around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you about another personality. Did you know a Becir Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I definitely know Becir Bogilovic from the beginning of the war. When we arrived in Srebrenica I was with my friend going around apartments and houses around Srebrenica to look for food or clothing, and I found a former, before-the-war police cap and I put on my head and I walked in the street. Bogilovic was walking up the road like a humongous figure waving his hands with a rifle in his hand and he shot off the cap off my head because I had a police cap on my head and then he was a police officer before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear about that, he shot the cap off your head. How old were you at this stage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was 13 years old when that happened. He shot it right off the top of my head, the cap, and if I didn't ran probably hit me or do whatever he want to with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain what if any his functions appeared to be at that time.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Srebrenica there was no police, there was no army, there was nothing there. There was no defence. As you can there is say there was soldiers walking down the street. The only authority that we could see was Bogilovic when he was walking around Srebrenica and higher authority around people, tell people what to do, where to go, how to do things and prevent people from going to the apartments or houses to look for food or clothing or whatever they can get.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It maybe stating the obvious, but I suppose he could have killed you when he shot.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, that was my first attempt by be so close to death. I mean I've been close to death before but not like -- immediately aiming at my head like he did and he could have definitely shot me right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I also want to ask you if you ever saw any sort of communication devices in the time that you were in the -- in the whole Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When I was in Srebrenica enclave during my time I saw communications, radios in the villages, Serbian villages. And when I found them, I found them missing with no battery or no antenna. They were basically destroyed so they could not be used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever come across anything described as Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found Motorolas and those basically like, today's standards, like a walkie-talkie, like, talk two three kilometres and they would be destroyed or no batteries or like I said other radios, basically useless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever try to use one of those devices?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I found it and I tried to use it I did not know I know the codes or whatever beepers. Basically with a walkie-talkie you press it talk on it basically it's not work. There is no batteries or destroyed not function. And if you were to use it in that area it's so rugged, so hilly, so mountainy [sic], basically it would be useless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in Mocevici were you aware of any fighters or other people using those devices to communicate with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. Just basic people, standing guard to protect the refugees and there was no radios, there was no uniforms, there was no weapons. You know, basic weapons like rifles, shotguns that were registered -- hunters had before war that were registered Serb, Serbs did not get to at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever go to a place called Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've got to Jezestica in the 1992 when late -- in late July sometimes in -- late summer-early fall in Jezestica when we heard there was going to be action very stronghold and myself and hundreds of other refugees went to the village above Jezestica, Jaglici and also another Sarancevici area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you've described yourself going with hundreds of other refugees. Was there any term given to you as a collectivity?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We were called torbari all times we were there, we refugees who were hungry, who would do anything for to regain -- to gain food and supplies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the torbari - and I'm just speaking generally now. If it's possible to answer generally - did they go in before fighters during the time that fighters were in actions, after, or what? Can you help us with that.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: With torbari you never know. There were thousands of us in the hills waiting to get supplies. So you can never know. If there was very fierce fighting going on like some of the villages some torbari would say look there is nothing happening there they are not going to be able to take over the village so torbari would go sneak in to burn a haystack or barn that they would send a signal to Serbs that something was burning so they would run. We've done -- I've done that before and other refugees would do anything just to get into village. They would go before, during the time of fighters and after.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, so going back to Jezestica, how did you actually learn that there was going to be an action there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Many people from that I know from Bratunac municipality from Voljevica from Zaluzje from Glogova our discussion that there was a very strong hold between Glogova and Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Pobrdje area very strong hold it must be taken. It's so strategically important because it's right in the centre connecting the Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Pobrdje and Srebrenica together with the Glogova area. And when we heard people talk and also many of the men the fighters lived in the homes, you know, and they would tell us, you know, tell the families, you know, tomorrow is going to be action be food. So one person would tell to another person and it would go all around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the day of this action, where exactly were you?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was in Jaglici, the hill -- the village above Jezestica. There with the other refugees and there was also a lot of refugees in torbari, in the Cizmici area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the result of that action?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The first attempt when we were there, that was not successful. Many were being carried wounded and dead but there was no success to take over that village. It was so strong hold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to people who participated in the action at any stage?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I spoke to couple of people from my village and I was there when they talked and they said it was so strong hold, so digged into the hills and to the ground with trenches, heavy weapons, it was impossible to take over and that particular village and that Serbs had rockets, they had tanks, they had cannons, they can shoot right back shelling where the Muslim areas are which we did not have to destroy their bunkers. That was the talk what I heard from my neighbours, my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again can you name some of the people who you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Enver from Voljevica, Mujo from Voljevica, those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they mention any specific places where some of the things you mentioned were located, tanks and artillery and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. All the Jezestica area the hills surrounding all around Jezestica Kravica and around towards Pobrdje and on towards Glogova all the hills around were surrounded with heavy weapons. It was impossible to get close to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there is a pause, it's because we need to slow down so you can just wait for a question. Did you yourself, when you went to Jezestica, did you see heavy artillery or anything that nature?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I could not see with my eye which or what artillery was but I could hear where it was coming from, from which hills, from which sides from -- where those shells were coming from. But I could not see with my own eye what weapon was shooting. But I could see where it was coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell us roughly what directions the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The shelling was coming from the main part of Kravica the shelling was coming from the Jezestica area and the fighting -- shells were coming from the hills separating Cizmici and Kravica that side and Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your conversations with people who participated in the action, did you get any information as to who was involved in it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. From people I spoke to, the situation was that the people from Bratunac municipality who were refugees in the Srebrenica area, they wanted to try to return to their homes, take over back their villages and it was very important to link the isolated area of Ceska to Glogova and then that part of Bratunac municipality. So basically from my talking to people it was people from Bratunac municipality and Glogova especially, led by Glogova people. And then other side there was Cerska and Konjevic Polje and Pobrdje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you speak about the people from Glogova, did they have any sort of a leader?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had. They had Ejub Golic who was the main leader who had his own group from Glogova and many other men from Bratunac municipalities joined his group to fight, to take over take back villages from Bratunac municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time, did you know many people from Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I know a lot of people from Glogova. My two friends were much older than I was, Refik and Senad from Glogova. And they would talk to me and they said our leader Ejub Golic is going to organise a force to take over Jezestica and Kravica area so we can return our people from Bratunac municipality to our own village and to our own municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can just pick up on what you said there, "so we can return our people from Bratunac municipality to our own village and to our own municipality," was there any sort of municipality loyalty or feelings or rivalry even between Bratunac municipality and Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, because the people that were expelled from their villages, from Bratunac municipality, they all arrived in Srebrenica area. And in Srebrenica area, there was people who were not expelled from their own villages. So people were refuge and they went to return to their own homes. So what they did is they wanted to return you know to Bratunac municipality, their villages and Srebrenica -- people from Srebrenica defended their own homes and it was a dispute going on, as we said. You know, Srebrenica defend your homes. We are going to go fight back our villages our homes to take them back so we don't have to be refugee forever in Srebrenica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, earlier in your testimony, you mentioned -- actually just to locate Jezestica you said it was late summer, are you able to be more precise as to the --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I would say it was probably maybe August, sometimes in August when that happened. August-September, that area. Or anywhere between late July and beginning of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you give us some sense of the numbers of people who were there on that action during that -- on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was a -- hundreds possibly even thousands torbari, refugees, all covered all around Jaglici and Cizmici area, all around the trees and woods and meadows waiting to descend into Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the summer of 1992, was there any other gathering in Jezestica of those numbers of people?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I understand your question. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other similar action in Jezestica in the summer of 1992 or was that the only one?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was attempts, you know, in -- I think there was a few attempts in Jezestica area also the total Glogova area there was a lot of attempts to take over Glogova to take it back from Serbs. Many actions that were taken in to take back Glogova were unsuccessful because the Glogova was in the centre between Bratunac and Kravica and the Serbs could have support coming from Bratunac or from Kravica. So it was impossible even if you get into Glogova to hold it for too long because it was a very strong presence of Serbian military in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier in your testimony, you mentioned Bjelovac. Did you -- did you go to Bjelovac after you had come to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've gone to Bjelovac during the action I believe was late 1992 sometimes I think in December when there was action in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Myself, together with thousands other people from Bratunac municipality or from whole area of Srebrenica, we knew that action was going to take place in Bjelovac and we knew that Bjelovac is a flat land close to the Drina River, same as our own villages of Voljevica, Zaluzje and that area and we knew that they have a vast amount of food. So for us to survive we had to go through the hills to Bjelovac to take whatever we can get for our own survival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you knew there would be a vast amount of food. Why did you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Because a lot of food for example from Voljevica Zaluzje were -- all our own goods were looted from by people from Bjelovac and from Pobrdje and was taken toward Bjelovac area and also because nice fertile land close to Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When is harvest time in your part of the world?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We have all different harvest time, you got corn you can do the -- have the corn in the springs and you got the -- I mean you got the flour that you harvest in the fall you get in spring. So you got all different times to do different harvesting in the area. Potato is different and beans and flour is different and corn and so on. So different harvesting. But not only food gets harvested, a lot of food in storage from our own villages were based in Bjelovac. Because we watched and it was taken from our villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were some of the places where people would store food?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Like outside -- outside storages. Many have outside like dig into the ground to keep food like in the hill, in the ground, outside storage and outside storages, they would have storages in the -- stuff in barns. They would have food in the house. They are everywhere all different kind of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before coming to the action in December, you told us how you went back to Voljevica before and how people were injured on those occasions. What are some of the way that is ha happened?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, in beginning of the war when we were attempting to go toward Voljevica, many people from my village that I know attempted to go through Biljaca and many of them were ambushed, many of them landmines, many of them were captured and never saw again. Even until this day they never know what happened to those people. And they were females, young men, old men, children, anybody. And then also when we attempted crossing from Srebrenica to Voljevica, the landmines were everywhere. And then of course shellings were continuous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you actually got into the town of Voljevica, were there ever any encounters when people went into larders or storage facilities?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, because most of it were looted from Voljevica but you would go whether people from Voljevica left Voljevica. They were hided outside somewhere with nobody can find it food. So I could not go to my house it was already burnt. I went to my neighbour's house. I know where he stored his food and I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going to Bjelovac now, can you describe for us the route you took to get down into Bjelovac and describe for us just briefly about what happened from your perspective during that action, what you saw. And not -- just so it's not too lengthy, you can start by just saying day by day what occurred and then we will take it more precisely.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: First day, we left hundreds and thousands of people from Srebrenica went toward Dimnici area. They were in that area and then from there I crossed to Pozlodnik area. That was on the first day. When the fierce fighting was -- first got to Dimnici the first amount of fighting was going down towards Bjelovac and Sase area and then I crossed over to Pozlodnik and I stayed there in the hills on the first day. On the first day this action was not successful. It was a fierce shelling, shooting fierce combat going down below and then you can hear shooting coming from Serbia and a lot of wounded and dead were being carried right past where we were in hills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the second day, I think. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: All during the first day was fighting going on and all through night and next day was also continuous fighting and sometimes in the -- in the morning hours, planes were bombing the area continuously, shelling was coming from Serbia, shelling was coming from Bratunac area, that direction. And fierce amount of fighting was going on especially on the hill above Bjelovac. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, please in the previous answer the witness gave I heard the witness say there was fist fighting going on as well which I thought might be a reference to hand-to-hand combat. So I think that needs to be clarified and it would be important that we get the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough, Mr. Di Fazio. In fact, that's what I thought I had heard too. But then of course, I was following also the transcript and I saw it was fierce in the transcript. So perhaps you can address that, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness has heard the exchange between Mr. Di Fazio and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Apart from the correction he has referred to fierce fighting and it might be useful just to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there close fighting, hand-to-hand combat in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: On the first day of fighting of combat there was not hand-to-hand combat. On the second day there was hand-to-hand combat in the village of Bjelovac, but on the first day when I was in the hills, there was fierce fighting going on down below. On the second day when we descended into Bjelovac that's where we saw hand-to-hand combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw that yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it clear enough now, Mr. Di Fazio? Thank you it has cleared up. Okay, let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that a hill by Bjelovac. Which hill is that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That would be Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Kunjerac on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I descended from the hills on to the Kunjerac and to Bjelovac. And my first arrival into Kunjerac was very dangerous was landmines were everywhere, there was bunkers, trenches, everywhere. When we got into the hill of Kunjerac there was a huge amount presence of rocket launchers, graffitis, Red Berets, all different weapons, and huge boxes, ammunition boxes filled with sand and digged very deeply into the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask: Why did you go up on Kunjerac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, when we descended from the Berisa hill, this is above Kunjerac down toward Kunjerac, it was the fastest way for me to get into Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you at this stage what were the numbers of people around? Were there a few, were there many?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When I got to Kunjerac together with other peoples, thousands of people in all directions, I can't be specific but I would say it was in the huge amount of thousands of people, everywhere. In every single direction you could look at you would see people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These fighters or civilians or what were they?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: This is starving civilians from Srebrenica, same as I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned airplanes. Did you see -- did you see with your own eyes the airplanes and did you see what if anything they were doing?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I saw the airplanes coming toward the Bratunac area into Serbia and then bombing all around Bjelovac area especially up toward Sikiric area that direction. The bombing was non-stop and that's where I think it was most fierce combat also was going on non-stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see where the bombs were falling from the planes?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Bombs were falling everywhere. A lot of bombs fell in the hills, lot a lot of bombs fell down low in the low grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say low grounds, are there any hamlets or villages which you remember?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: If you go to Bjelovac from the centre of the village toward up toward toward the Loznicka Rijeka, that area. A lot of bombs were falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the hamlets and villages beyond Loznicka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I know the names of the villages of that area but I have not gone there much. Jovanovici, Sikiric, Loznicka Rijeka, that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so did you see any bombs falling in those areas, Jovanovici, Sikirici or not?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's where most of the bombs went, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One question and this is not relating to the day but just generally when you are in Bjelovac can you actually see Sikiric, can you see people in Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: You could not see from Bjelovac Sikiric, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Because you had the curved road and you've got hills between. You cannot see Sikiric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you eventually go into Bjelovac yourself? I think you told us you did.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I descended down to the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you firstly describe for us what if anything you saw there in terms of military hardware.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen down by on the bank of the Drina there was two APCs right on the bank and there was a shooting, furious shooting coming from Serbia blocking protecting those two APCs. And I saw weapons everywhere. And I saw a tractor full of weapons taken from Bjelovac toward Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know who drove that tractor?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The guy's name -- he's from my village. His name is Mujic. He drove that truck full of grenades, anti-aircraft gun and bullets. All different kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for the next set of questions I'd actually like to go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a while, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We shall in open session, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, give me a moment. You said a lot of stuff was going on that was lit on fire from the combat. Can you explain that just a little more what you bean by houses being set on fire from the combat.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In Bjelovac, this on second day there was a hand-to-hand combat so if Muslim forces go into the one house, few metres away there is a Serbian soldiers in that house so the Serbian soldiers would be using Zoljas or RPGs or anything that is available to them to knock out the Muslim fighters from the house next -- next to where they are. So when they hit the house they will hit the wall and automatically start house on fire and also many shells were landing on top of the house and the roof automatically pick up fire, those houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why could you say they would automatically start on fire when a shell landed?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: For those who haven't seen or haven't been so close to when a shell falls or when a Zolja hits it destroys everything right away, and it's so much flame, so much fire, so much fragments flying around so there is no way not to start it on fire. It's a huge flame. And especially when a tank shell lands on top of the house, it destroys everything right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you reached the centre of Bjelovac, did you see fighters, if you understand or if you attach any meaning to that? Were there any fighters, recognisable fighters, there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: As the torbari were arriving in Bjelovac, you could see fighters pulling back out of Bjelovac and we were left to take whatever we wanted to take for what was in need for us for Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they were pulling back, at that stage, were houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was not houses on fire, own couple of places we saw where there was combat, fierce combat you could see on fire there. Not regular house on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were the -- why were the fighters pulling back, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: It's obvious reason. Whenever there is action they take they go into action they take -- if the village is taken over, then there is no reason to stay there. Besides, there is the so far from the area, you can not even hold the area so the refugees go in there. So the basic reason is take those villages is for people to get supplies. So when they successfully took over the village then the refugees descend on it take what they like and move out also. There is no reason for them to stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do I understand from that that you didn't see any intention to remain and occupy Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not because we did not want -- there is no reason to take their villages, only the reason that we go into action is take what's ours return to our own homes, not to tabling nobody else's home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stop here for a moment because I think this needs to be cleared up a little bit. Did the torbari descend into or onto Bjelovac once the fighting had stopped and the soldiers were already retreating or did the torbari descend while fighting was still ongoing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, both times. During the fighting and after the fighters pulled back, you will see torbari because for example I'll see my neighbour. He was getting sack of corn on his back the action was still going on down there. And we asked him how did you do that he goes I went myself down there and got it. So with torbari during, before and after. When there was -- torbari were killed that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what we need to have some further information about is you were asked by Mr. Jones whether there were houses burning at the time when the soldiers were retreating. Could you give us a description exactly, an exact description, or as nearly an exact description as possible as to what was the picture at the time when the soldiers were withdrawing as regards burning or destruction of houses at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a few house that is were burning where you can see where the shelling, that fierce fighting was going on and you could see where the shells were knocked right through the wall on top of the house and that house on fire, two or three guys saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, if you were to count all these houses, how many houses would you say you saw destroyed or burning at the time you descended into Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The time we arrived I saw probably about 3 houses, 2, 3 houses where the combat was going on where there was huge holes in the houses. That's only ones I saw, about three or four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this would be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- in which part of Bjelovac? In the direction of Loznicka Rijeka, or...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of Loznicka Rijeka, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Eser, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a further question just to clarify the situation. You spoke of a fierce combat. Now, combat between whom? And when there was a combat between fighters, where have the torbari been? Have they been in between or around? And could you describe this a little bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Best way to describe imagine two houses in the village, in one house there is a Serbian soldiers, and in the other's house there is Muslim fighters and you can see hand-to-hand -- the RPG, the Zoljas shooting at the area where the Muslim fighters were, trying to knock them out of Bjelovac out of the houses. So when they were shooting the RPGs and Zoljas and the shells at the house where the Muslim fighters were you could see right -- because every house was up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: In such a situation, where have been the torbaris?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Torbaris everywhere. You can never see where tobaris are. Like animals, flying in every single direction. They can be in between Serbs and Muslims. They can be already stealing food. They can be already burning haystacks or whatever they can get to. There was no -- there was no way to know where torbari were. They were everywhere. Just like releasing a flock of birds in every single direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But wasn't it very dangerous to be in between both sides? So could it happen that torbaris to even have been killed by their own fighters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our lives when we were expelled from our village and on rest of the time were very dangerous. Every single move you're close to death and when you were in Bjelovac it was nothing new. Death is present at all times regardless where you're at whether you're in Bjelovac or Srebrenica or anywhere. So it's possible -- not possible, it's true that many torbari were killed that way. It was for them to die from starvation or to hunt for food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones. Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm leaving Bjelovac now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I did want to come back to Hazim Mercury whom you mentioned. Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Hazim, I believe it's Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: He -- him and his mother were very good with my family so he came to see my father very often before war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he live before the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: His family came from Jeskovica which is municipality of Srebrenica and moved to Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war did you see him in Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've seen around the village. I've been to his house in Voljevica. He came to my house in Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe a little what he was like, his personality.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Hazim was a nice guy. He was a very friendly to everybody. He moved around our village. He was maybe a little bit taller than me, very nice build.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you told us which unit he was in during the war.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was first in Hakija Meholjic and later on he was with Akif Ustic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he bear a resemblance to anyone?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. If you were in Srebrenica and many times when he came to the house and if you look at him ten metres away or 20 metres away you will say it's exactly Naser Oric, a hundred per cent copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any incidents in that regard?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I was on Konjevic Polje once and also in Suceska area and he would go around and he will -- because if you never saw Naser or if you never saw Hazim and if he say I'm Naser Oric everybody looks and says, Oh, maybe it is. If you look so he did many things. He will say, Give me this or that, I'm Naser, and people would give it to him. And he liked the attention to be Naser.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry if I took that slightly out of sequence. There is a reason. I do actually have a couple more questions about Bjelovac. From your conversations with people from any other source of information, did you learn who participated in the action in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. It was people from that area, people from Voljevica, people from Zaluzje, Bjelovac, Biljaca, that area who wanted to go back to toward our own villages. Those were Bratunac people from Bratunac municipality and were -- there was a Mido [phoen] there was from Biljaca and people who were expelled from that area who wanted to return their homes and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in fact we might not have even entirely finished with Bjelovac. How long -- how long did you in fact stay in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: You cannot stay in Bjelovac for too long because Bjelovac was right on the border on the bank of the Drina River and from Serbia, from there, tanks shelling, there was anti-aircraft continuously shooting. There was -- you could not go down, you had to stay very close to the road. And there was a lot of shelling coming from the Sikiric area and then from Bratunac area there was continuously attacks in Bjelovac. So as soon as you go there grab whatever you can get and try to run out of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, while we are still on Bjelovac, particularly the witness could explain to us the various actions as they occurred or they happened according to him, depending on whether it was morning or afternoon on the relevant day or days. I'm leaving the choice of questions of course entirely to you, but you know exactly why I am asking these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or asking to you ask these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if you heard His Honour's request for clarification. Perhaps a way to take it is when you were actually in Bjelovac itself, what time of day was it when you first got into the town?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I went to Bjelovac on the second day around mid-day or so into Bjelovac. And there were people before me who were down in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to airplanes. Whether did you see those?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: On the second days in the morning times I could see the airplanes flying when I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of airplanes did you see? I meant to ask you that earlier.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, the time there was two what we called two propeller planes or two-wing planes and there was also another one we call coach planes, agricultural planes flying above the head bombing the area around Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait a moment. I see coach planes. It's agricultural planes, as I take it. These are airplanes that arrive for spring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were used before the war as agricultural planes and there is another one with two wings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Biplanes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Biplanes. There you go, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see other planes or aircraft in that area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later on when we tried to my sister and I tried to go back to Voljevica to gain food, there was fighter planes flying from Serbia area, from Bratunac area -- in Serbia from Bratunac, that direction, and other side of Drina going towards Bjelovac and bombing continuously that area. That was not a small planes that were bombing on the second day. That was fighter actual fighter planes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did you see the fighter planes, what time of day?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Mid-day probably noon or so, sometime that time, mid-day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that on the same day, the second day as you're describing it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The second day when I saw those biplanes and those planes bombing I saw them but a few days after I tried to attempt to go to Voljevica I saw the mixed bombed area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then still on the second day, how long did you stay in Bjelovac on the second day? And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I stayed around Bjelovac for the rest of the day and from there we moved out and then myself I moved out towards Srebrenica and towards Srebrenica. But many people stayed in that area. You could not go -- you could not stay very close to Drina bank because there was non-stop fighting coming from Serbia shooting into Bosnian part, to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see shells or any other missiles actually landing in Bjelovac from -- being shot from the other side of the Drina?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, because when the fighters pulled out, the -- the Serbian artillery was positioned outside Serbia and was continually bombing the Bjelovac area it could be -- the bombing could be a Serbian house or Muslim house or Roma house, did not look what was there when they were bombing, when they were shelling that area. They not only shelled Bjelovac area they shelled up towards Sikiric and they shelled up towards Biljaca and Sase area, that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us how you put out towards Sase. Did you actually manage to get any food or provisions yourself?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I was young, you know, and I could not carry very much so my main thing is find what is more useful in Srebrenica, like tobacco, cigarettes tobacco, sugar and coffee I find that and take it and exchange it for food flour or corn. I found it in Bjelovac and I take it back to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then was the second day, was that the end of the action in Bjelovac or were you aware of anything else happening after that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the so-called end of the -- end of the action but it was never a liberated -- liberated, say okay we can move freely I was continuously after that fighting in the Bjelovac you know till Serbs took over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move on to another action because you mentioned you saw several. Did you -- did you ever go back to the Jezestica area first of all?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've gone back there in January 1993, that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an action or was it something else?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That was the action when the action was in Jezestica and Kravica and that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know beforehand that there would be an action or did you just find out?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Everybody in Srebrenica knew there was going to be action as soon as the other villagers -- men will be, you know, stay in their home and they will be telling their families what was going on. And I heard from my friends that action will be taking place in Kravica and then together with thousands of other refugees from Srebrenica I went towards Jaglici area and many other refugees went towards Pale, Zimice, that area also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay. Just give a moment for the interpretation. First I'm going to ask you what you were wearing that day.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I have the jeans and a sweater, jacket with the white sheet rope over me and that was the routine that we wore, torbari especially, in the winter we would take any bed sheeting or any kind of white sheet like a robe and then we wrapped -- put it over all our clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, simple reason: Because theres' snow and if you moving around if you don't have something white on you you're like black figures around snow and they can spot you from every single direction. This way if I have a robe on me, they can't see me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just describe for us first of all just overall what you did that day, where you went and what you saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. He's mentioning snow. Which action is he referring to in particular now? Because I suppose it couldn't have been Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, we had moved on to Jezestica. He said he went back there in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. All right. Was he there in August as well or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's our submission. He said late summer late July early August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's exactly what I understood. Would there be snow on the hills in the mountains there?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, no this is the second occasion we are talking about, January 1993. We can clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need to because otherwise, this snow business and wearing white clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- the action you talked about when you went up to Jaglici in the summer, what were you wearing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: We talk about in late July and August sometime?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Normal clothes what I can get on you, you can be jeans or sweater or T-shirt, you know. But in the one I'm talking about now when it comes to snow it's January 1993 in the Kravica attack in the Jezestica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give a brief overview of where you went and what you saw on that occasion, January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: When we arrived from Srebrenica, to Jaglici and all surrounding areas it was a fierce cold winter. When we got there was an action going on down below in Jezestica and Kravica area. Thousands of torbari were everywhere around the hills in the trees with the fires and preparing to descend down into Kravica. Myself, I descended from Jaglici down into Kajici area and I stayed there and I got into Kravica. In Kravica I could see -- first of all we got to one house, there was a -- and then there it was a spray of machine-gun coming from the window and then we hid and then was probably 50 kilometres -- 50 metres from the house, and we hid behind a haystack and then the next thing you heard was a huge explosion, like a grenade, and then we got to the house there there was a two dead bodies, two older people, old people, with a machine-gun right next to them. They were dead there. And then from there I moved down to the centre of the village. I saw APC moving very slowly, shooting continuously all around the hills and I saw "four-barrel anti-aircraft on a hill in Srebrenica -- in the centre of Kravica upon a hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I just stop you there, just to go back a little bit when you said that thousands of torbari were everywhere around the hills in the trees with the fires and preparing to descend down into Kravica." Can you explain or clarify what exactly you were referring to there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, what I mean is we were starved and what we wanted to do is gain food from Kravica and many attempts were made to go down and when the fierce fighting was going on we couldn't descend. And then later on when we saw the combat getting worse and worse then everybody else, everybody, even torbari went straight down to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, but when you it were referring to fires in the hills and the trees?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that you were referring to there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That's to heat ourselves, you know. We were waiting and we wanted to make a little fire to heat your hands, stay around fire. All of us who were freezing in the snow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see many similar fires in that area before the action?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: A lot of fires in the Jaglici area, people who are trying to heat themselves up, a lot of fires in that area. People squatting right next to a fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned how you had this white sheet on you. Can you estimate how many other torbari were wearing something similar?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Majority of torbari were wearing something like that because we had the idea you don't go into any kind of -- whether it was action or anything or non -- especially in the winter, unless you take something to cover yourself which is white. Everybody had that. Majority of people had that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, when we are talking about the torbari, do you know where they were from, the torbari, what places?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Majority of people that were there were all Bratunac municipality people who were refuge. For those you know for Srebrenica people who had their homes not burned completely, they stayed back and they can harvest something in their own backyard, their own land, but when we were expelled from Bratunac municipality we had nothing. So the majority of those people, those starving people that were already expelled from their villages from Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you referred to artillery firing. Can you describe roughly the locations and if you saw anything, you know, what types of artillery were firing that day.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, there is the from the hills I believe it's called Zeleni it's toward Drina there was a strong shelling coming from that area into Kravica when still action was going on down there. Huge shelling was coming from there from all other hills around toward Drina from if you go from Konjevic Polje left side in the hills toward Drina and then from Glogova area also on the Drina side was coming into Kravica, all different shelling. And then also in Kravica there was four-barrel, like I say, on a hill. There was continuously mobbing the area in all around in the Kravica. So he could be actually shooting at his own people or he could be shooting at the Muslims in the Kravica area. Same thing with shells that were coming into Kravica area. They could be shelling their own people, their own houses and at Muslims that were in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mention this four-barrel. What exactly is that? That's something which perhaps you can help us with, having not seen one.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well we called that praga, I don't know how would say in English. It would be like four-barrel anti-aircraft cannons, I guess that's how it would translate. But I'm not sure that's the military term for it. If a sense you shoot sort of like shells all around the area, not as big shells as a regular cannon or tank but it's like sprays at one time four barrels shooting non-stop, from all four barrels at once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first time you'd seen such a weapon or had you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I've seen that before. I've seen that in Bjelovac I've seen that in other villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you may not be able to say for each hill where artillery was firing from but can you give us an idea at least roughly how many different locations you were aware that there was artillery firing from?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Artillery fire was coming from at least five six different directions different hills right into Kravica and that was the same time as the combat was going on and I was -- and together with the other torbari right in the village and it was continuously coming shells and even Serbs were in those houses still. Their soldiers and our fighters and civilians were in the village at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know a location called Siljkovici?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I know where Siljkovici -- I know Siljkovici but I was not in Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day were you aware of anything happening there or anything located there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Fierce combat was and fierce fighting was going on in Siljkovici area. I heard that but I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know, then, that there was combat there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Because you can hear people saying there is a humongous fighting going on Siljkovici and you can hear also the huge shells coming from that direction, explosions that area that was coming also toward Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know or did you find out about what was captured in Kravica in terms of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I saw a lot of ox carts carrying a lot of heavy weapons, anti-aircraft guns, a lot of shells, lot of rocket launchers, multi-rocket launchers were all being carried by ox carts toward Jaglici area. And extremely a lot of light weapons like automatic rifle, AK-47, machine-gun, that kind of guns, a lot of it. And then also when I was coming out of Kravica you can see a hill that is between Zimice and Kravica and it's got a lot of those small rocket -- rockets, RPGs, all around the hills everywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were you actually doing on that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I trust he didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: He did not shoot her, no. He slapped her and he screamed at her and told some stuff and there was nothing else he can do. And then you can also see when the shells were coming, when the -- were coming into Kravica like I said in Bjelovac there would land on top of the house and house was right away flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm mindful of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is not going to be a next break, actually, because we understand that the witness requires 30 minutes in any case by way of a break and if we stop at quarter past 1 and have a 30 minute break that would take us to quarter to 2 when we are supposed to finish. So you have these options. You are either finish at five minutes time or we recuperate the seven, eight minutes that we lost after the last break and of course you lose the credit at the same time, and maybe you close one of the chapters or -- that you will dealing with now and we continue tomorrow. It's up to you, Mr. Jones. We are not going to make it difficult for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think I can finish today. That would be preferable. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean you finish today?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps I misunderstood Your Honour. I can keep going for half an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Keep going or half an hour I think we need the okay from the interpreters and the technical staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Fine with the interpreters, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Fine with the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine with the interpreters. I don't know whether it's fine with the technicians, and of course I need or we need to make sure that the witness himself agrees to this, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I understand that he needs to walk the dog.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the last thing I would do is to create difficulties for this witness who has been very cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I'm just looking again at my notes. I think I can finish in 15 minutes if that's -- if that's okay with the witness, if it's okay with everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that it won't cause you any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Suppose if it is so short and we stop now we will still be confident to finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, okay. Would it be all right with you, Mr. Bekric, if we continued for another 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jones and I wish to -- I haven't heard from the technicians as yet. It's okay. All right. So I wish to acknowledge again our gratitude to both the technicians and the interpreters. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few more questions, Mr. Bekric, on Kravica then we are almost done. On that day did you see damage to property that was actually caused by shells or other missiles?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've seen quite a few houses that were destroyed by shelling or other military equipment the Serbs used or -- that were shelled at the at the houses, houses, barns, other -- things in the Kravica area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Jones, I'm just taking the initiative, I'm sure that Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser would agree with me, to order -- Mr. Jones, to redact the transcript in the relative parts when he just went out of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will do it under our own responsibility and proceed go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go into many houses on that day?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what if anything did you find in those houses?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: In those houses, the first house I mentioned I saw the two old bodies. I saw machine-gun, I saw all different things in the house, and the houses I went into you can see the old houses were full of stuff you wanted. You could see a lot of small weapons and a lot of grenades, a lot of military equipment around those houses. And I took whatever I wanted from those houses and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself find any military equipment or anything like that? Sorry, let me rephrase that. Did you actually take anything of a military nature yourself?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not take anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Serbs fighting back in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I could see where the combat was taking place but I could not see them with my own eye to say specifically who I saw. But I could see combat was going on in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you name some of the places the Serbs were fighting from?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes. The main combat where I was at was the main part of Kravica. You could see the fierce combat, huge explosions going on in the villages around. But in the where -- I saw the main part of Kravica house-to-house combat and you can see huge explosions, you know, when they hit the house the house goes right away up into had air. It was coming towards Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Serbs fighting from trenches or from their houses or in the streets or what?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, Serbs used a lot of tricks. They were smart. They would shoot many of us as civilians. They would -- the front lines were they would pull from there and go into their houses and they keep silent. And then you think nobody is there so you run very fast into the house. They start shooting with the machine-guns, with the grenades, with the RPGs with the Zoljas actually right there. So they used a lot of -- they used the houses as their way to fight back. They would surprise you. They would go up on top roof, the balcony, keep silent. If you're coming they'll just spray you with a machine gun or whatever weapons they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that something which you yourself experienced or you saw or you heard about?
