utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I've seen that myself. Like I said, the first one I saw the machine-gun shooting from the window and then same thing down in main part of Kravica you could see especially in the new houses, the bigger houses. They would use balconies, and shoot from balconies with whatever weapons they had at the people, whether civilian or a fighter. Whoever was coming toward them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kravica that day?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I stayed all through the day in Kravica. And took whatever I wanted and I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you in fact take?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I took 25 kilos of flour. I could not carry it so I took a lid at the wooden stove and I put it on and I pulled behind me on snow. And I took -- I also found camouflage pants inside the house and I took them and put over my pants. And I also found a pair of boots and I put them on and I sold my camouflage pants I found for a bottle of plum brandy so I can exchange it for food in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of the day, how many houses if you're able to say or what proportion of houses in Kravica did you see damaged?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. This sentence redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you obtain any information at any stage about which units or which fighters were involved in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. It was Golic, Ejub Golic from Glogova who led the attack because he was, from the stories from the talks from people that I know from Glogova and from Voljevica and that area, it was very important first of all for food and also strategically very important because we had an isolated area of Cerska and Konjevic Polje Pobrdje area was totally isolated and had a very strong hold of -- Serbian stronghold in Kravica it would be very important for Golic to take that over in order to connect Glogova together with Cerska, isolated area of Cerska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not people from Cerska or Konjevic Polje participated in the action?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I presume they would -- they participated in the action from the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Pobrdje several times. Unfortunately that doesn't appear on our map. Can you name a village or hamlet in that area so we can locate it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yeah, Lozica, Sandici, Pervani, Burnice. That area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've spoken already about attempts of people to return to return to Glogova in this period. As far as you know, were those attempts successful?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Those attempts were, you know, they were, the fighters would go into Glogova have a they could not hold it whatsoever for long because the support that was coming, the support from Bratunac, the support from Kravica that was coming to Serbs was impossible to hold it because of all the counterattacks and stuff in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned counterattacks. Can you explain at all what if anything you observed or knew about Serbian counterattacks and how that was carried out.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't in Glogova but from people that I know from Glogova that spoke to us they would say they were going to Glogova and get into Glogova and then we counterattack from Serbian forces from Bratunac for Kravica and right away knocked them out, kill whoever was in their counterattacks from Bratunac from Kravica area and from where I was they call cleaning the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was no way to hold it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know if that happened after this action in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: That happened quite often in even before and after because after Kravica was taken over, Golic and his men of course tried to hold Glogova and it was impossible to hold even then and then the counterattacks were continuously coming from Bratunac area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to Kravica after the action?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I've gone to Kravica after the action and I've seen Kravica after the action. I had an aunt that lived in that village of Burnice which is in Pobudje [Realtime transcript read in error: "Pobrdje"] and I went through Kravica into Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why apart from -- was that the only reason, going to see your aunt or was there another reason for going there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was a reason to go see my aunt so I could get from her see -- she did not move from her own village, so I hoping to gain food from her and to go to see them, you know. Both reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just for the transcript page 94, line 18, there is a place called Pobrdje but the witness is referring to which is Pobudje. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you passed through Kravica after the action, what if anything did you see occurring in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see people from surrounding villages, from Lolici, Sandici, that area in Kravica taking tile roof tiles taking the windows, doors, blocks from the houses, whatever they can get from the houses in Kravica to take it to their homes and rebuild their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why they were rebuilding their homes?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there very much before Kravica fell so I don't know what's going on, but a lot from the shellings from the bombings, from the burnings. That would be the reason. I definitely saw them take stuff from Kravica into their villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned being in Srebrenica when General Morillon was there. I'm only going to ask you this about that. You recollect General Morillon coming to Srebrenica. My question is, is this, it's a general question: How vividly do you remember the events of which you've spoken this morning?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: The events I spoke about this morning is events I'll never forget in my life. Every single detail of it. And I'll always remember those. That's the last things I saw and last things I'll always remember. Every single detail of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, finally, you explained at the beginning that the shelling which occurred in which I think you said 60 or something children were killed in fact. Can you help us with that? Do you know how many people were killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: My understanding there was about 60, 62 people killed on that day and there was over 100 wounded on that day. The UN peacekeepers weren't in there at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear if there was ever any investigation into the massacre on the soccer field?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BEKRIC
utterances.text: There was never an investigation that I know. There was no plaque that marks anything that the massacre happened on that field. There is no sign of anything to say this is what happened at the soccer field. Nobody -- just forgot it like it never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we have an exhibit which is the newspaper -- is a newspaper article dated 29 September 2002, St. Petersburg Times. I'm just dealing with that just for the record, I think it's useful to submit. I believe the Prosecution has already seen a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask if that could be given a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. By all means. This will be Defence Exhibit D71 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 3, yes. And that is an article from St. Petersburg Times entitled "Hope for change seen amid tale of tragedy." By Mary Jane Park, consisting of two pages and in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. That completes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. St. Petersburg, where would this be? I would take it that it is some St. Petersburg, somewhere in the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I believe it's Florida but the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a city where I went to school in Florida.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. So I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour, I also propose to tender the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It hasn't been in issue but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't -- but if there is no point in asking the witness to initialise it in any case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can initial it, Your Honour. I can put my two letters if needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it is needed. We will just give it a number and this will be D714. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bekric.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think that concludes today's sitting. You will need to return tomorrow, Mr. Bekric, in the morning. We have sitting starting hopefully at 9.00 in Trial Chamber II, if I am not mistaken. And tomorrow you will be cross-examined by Mr. Wubben who is lead counsel for the Prosecution. Do you expect to finish your cross-examination tomorrow, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Basically that means we will finish there. We won't have anyone on Friday or for Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We stand adjourned. Please make sure that the witness is given all the assistance he requires. Thank you. Good afternoon to everyone.
